Modal Verbs for Speculating and Talking about Possibility
When you speculate about something, you are making an assumption based on what you know about the situation.

You can show you are speculating about something by using a modal, like must or have got to.
You can also speculate using can't and couldn't.
For example: John is always online. He must not have access to wi-fi.   >> we know something about John so we can make an assumption about why he is not online.
An assumption is an “educated guess”. You make an assumption when you already have some information about the situation.
To talk about something that is possible you use might, may and could.
For example: We should call his mobile phone. There may be a problem with the wi-fi. >> we don't know about the wi-fi so we have to talk about what is possible, or make a guess.
The modal verb is followed by the main verb in the base form. You do not use “to”. Do not add “ing”, “ed”, or “s” to the verb.
Something must be happening to Ferdinand.
It could be a bad connection.
He might not have access to wi-fi.
Could we possibly have a disgruntled competitor?

A gerund is a verb ending with -ing (doing).
An Infinitive is to + verb (to do).

There are rules about which verbs you can use with gerunds and which verbs you can use with Infinitives.
These structures give more information about how you feel about an action.
Verbs commonly followed by a gerund:

like
love
enjoy
dislike
hate
can't stand
Example:
I can't stand calling him and reaching his voicemail.
NOTE: like/love can also be followed by an initiative.

images.text:
Secretary: Miss Ellison, something must be happening to Ferdinand. It could be a bad connection.
Janet: Has he tried contacting me more than once? Wait, he might not have access to wi-fi.
Secretary: There's this one voice message. But he kept on calling from his cellphone. Allow me to replay it.
Answering machine: “Janet, I apologize for being absent, but we really need to chat. Pretty serious matter. It could jeopardize everything ... ”

Secretary: Sounds like there might be an emergency vehicle and then it cuts out.
Janet: It could be an ambulance. An accident? He may be hurt.
Miranda: I've know him for a while. He tends to avoid getting in trouble. He should be fine.
Janet: Could this be related to the event?
Miranda: It can't be. I'd be surprised since things came off really well. What may have changed? You've tried calling, right?
Janet: Yes, repeatedly. I can't stand calling him and reaching his voicemail. It's full and I can't leave a message. I wonder if he could be experiencing financial difficulties.

Miranda: It can't be that. He proposed not making any financial negotiations during that time. Could we possibly have a disgruntled competitor?
Janet: That is a possibility.
Miranda: Janet ... ummm ... I would hesitate to contact Farmani until we hear from Ferdinand.
Janet: Absolutely not. Anyway, I urge you to spend the morning trying to contact him.
Miranda: I plan on doing that. And ... ummm ... Janet, Ferdinand has good work ethics, I'm sure everything is under control. I'll keep calling!
